cashTip: US dollars are used alongside riel for change; carry small notes. Tipping is welcome.
name: Kampot
tagline: Riverside town of pepper farms and Bokor mountain
summary: Kampot is a sleepy riverside town of faded French shophouses in southern Cambodia. Visit the farms that grow world-famous Kampot pepper, ride up to the eerie abandoned hill station on Bokor Mountain, paddle the river at sunset to see fireflies, and eat fresh crab with green pepper in nearby Kep.
seasonNote: November to March is dry; the rainy season (June to October) is green but wet.
arrival: Buses and minivans from Phnom Penh take 3 to 4 hours; there is also a slow train.
gettingAround: Rent a scooter or hire a tuk-tuk for pepper farms, Bokor and Kep.
foodTip: Kep crab with Kampot green pepper, fish amok and durian.

items.name: Bokor National Park
items.summary: Abandoned French hill station with a ghostly church and old casino in the clouds.
items.expect: Scooter or tour; cooler on top.
items.tip: Go on a clear morning.

items.name: Kampot pepper farms
items.summary: Farms growing protected-origin Kampot pepper, with free tours and tastings.
items.tip: La Plantation offers free tours.

items.name: Sunset river cruise and fireflies
items.summary: Boat up the Praek Tuek Chhu river at sunset, then fireflies in the mangroves.
items.tip: Pick a boat that stays for the fireflies.

items.name: Kampot old town
items.summary: French colonial shophouses, the old bridge and the durian roundabout.
items.tip: Walk at golden hour.

items.name: Kep crab market and beach
items.summary: Seaside town with a crab market where women pull crabs from baskets in the sea.
items.tip: Eat crab with green pepper on the wooden decks.

items.name: Phnom Chhngok cave temple
items.summary: 7th-century brick temple inside a limestone cave.
items.expect: Small fee; a local child may guide you.
items.tip: Bring a torch.

items.name: Kep crab with green pepper
items.summary: Stir-fried crab with fresh green Kampot peppercorns.
items.tip: Eat at the crab market stalls.

items.name: Fish amok
items.summary: Steamed curried fish custard in banana leaf.
items.tip: Pair with jasmine rice.

items.name: Kampot night market
items.summary: Evening stalls with grills, fruit shakes and snacks.
items.tip: Try a fresh fruit shake.

cashTip: Cards and e-wallets work in malls; carry cash for hawker stalls. No tipping.
name: Ipoh
tagline: Cave temples, street art and white coffee
summary: Ipoh is a laid-back tin-mining city famous across Malaysia for its food. Wander the old town's heritage shophouses and street murals, visit Buddhist temples built inside limestone caves, sip the original Ipoh white coffee, and eat bean sprout chicken and silky tau fu fa. The Cameron Highlands tea plantations are two hours away.
seasonNote: Warm all year; afternoon storms are common in the wetter months.
arrival: ETS trains from Kuala Lumpur take about 2 hours 15 minutes.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; Grab to cave temples.
foodTip: Ipoh white coffee, bean sprout chicken (nga choi kai), hor fun, tau fu fa and dim sum.
buyTip: White coffee and heong peng biscuits.

items.name: Kek Lok Tong
items.summary: Cave temple opening onto a garden of lakes beneath limestone cliffs.
items.tip: Walk through to the garden behind.

items.name: Sam Poh Tong
items.summary: Ipoh's oldest cave temple with a hidden Japanese garden and turtle pond.
items.tip: Walk through the cave to the hidden garden.

items.name: Old Town and Mural Art Lane
items.summary: Heritage shophouses and murals by Ernest Zacharevic.
items.tip: Follow the mural map.

items.name: Concubine Lane
items.summary: Narrow lane of restored shophouses with snacks and souvenirs.
items.tip: Try the tau fu fa here.

items.name: Kellie's Castle
items.summary: Unfinished mansion of a Scottish planter in the jungle.
items.tip: Look for the rumoured secret tunnels.

items.name: Ipoh Railway Station
items.summary: Grand white colonial station nicknamed the Taj Mahal of Ipoh.
items.tip: Photograph from the Birch Memorial side.

items.name: Cameron Highlands
items.summary: Cool hills of tea plantations and mossy forest.
items.tip: Visit BOH Sungei Palas tea estate.

items.name: Ipoh white coffee
items.summary: Coffee beans roasted in palm-oil margarine, served with condensed milk.
items.tip: Sin Yoon Loong and Nam Heong are the classic shops.

items.name: Bean sprout chicken
items.summary: Poached chicken with fat local bean sprouts and hor fun noodles.
items.tip: Lou Wong is the famous one.

items.name: Dim sum breakfast
items.summary: Huge dim sum halls opening at dawn.
items.tip: Foh San and Ming Court are famous.

cashTip: Carry rupiah for boats and warungs; cards work in hotels. Tipping is appreciated.
name: Labuan Bajo (Komodo)
tagline: Komodo dragons, pink beaches and manta rays
summary: Labuan Bajo is a harbour town on Flores and the gateway to Komodo National Park. Take a boat to see wild Komodo dragons on Rinca or Komodo island, hike Padar Island for its three-bay view, swim on a pink-sand beach, and snorkel or dive with manta rays in some of the world's richest reefs.
seasonNote: April to October is dry; July and August are busiest; seas are rougher from December to March.
arrival: Flights from Bali take about 1 hour.
gettingAround: Day boats or liveaboards into the park; walk the town.
foodTip: Grilled fish at the night market, Flores coffee and Indonesian classics.

items.name: Komodo dragons on Rinca or Komodo
items.summary: See the world's largest lizards with a ranger on a guided walk.
items.tip: Go in the morning when the dragons are active.

items.name: Padar Island viewpoint
items.summary: Climb to a ridge above three bays of white, black and pink sand.
items.tip: Go at sunrise.

items.name: Pink Beach
items.summary: Beach tinted pink by red coral, with good snorkelling.
items.tip: Snorkel the reef off the beach.

items.name: Manta Point
items.summary: Snorkel or dive with manta rays in strong currents.
items.expect: Currents are strong; for confident swimmers.
items.tip: Go with a dive shop or reputable boat.

items.name: Kanawa Island
items.summary: Small island with clear water and turtles over the reef.
items.tip: Snorkel the drop-off.

items.name: Sylvia Hill sunset
items.summary: Hill above town with sunset over the islands.
items.tip: Bring water.

items.name: Cunca Wulang waterfall
items.summary: Jungle waterfall with a canyon pool for swimming.
items.tip: Wear water shoes.

items.name: Kampung Ujung night market
items.summary: Waterfront stalls grilling fresh fish and squid.
items.tip: Choose your fish and agree the price first.

items.name: Flores coffee
items.summary: Bajawa coffee grown in the Flores highlands.
items.tip: Buy beans to take home.

items.name: Nasi campur and sate
items.summary: Rice with mixed dishes from warungs.
items.tip: Point at what you want.

cashTip: UPI is everywhere but foreign cards may not link; carry rupees for small places and taxis. Tip about 10 percent in restaurants.
name: Darjeeling
tagline: Tea gardens, the toy train and Kangchenjunga at dawn
summary: Darjeeling is a Himalayan hill station on a ridge facing Kangchenjunga, the world's third-highest mountain. Watch sunrise light the peaks from Tiger Hill, ride the UNESCO toy train, tour tea estates and taste first-flush Darjeeling, and wander the Mall and Tibetan monasteries.
seasonNote: October and November give the clearest mountain views; monsoon (June to September) brings cloud and landslides.
arrival: Fly to Bagdogra or take a train to New Jalpaiguri, then 3 hours by shared jeep or car.
gettingAround: Walk the ridge; taxis for Tiger Hill and tea estates.
foodTip: Momos, thukpa, Tibetan bread and of course Darjeeling tea.
baseArea: Near the Chowrasta and the Mall

connections.note: Fly to Bagdogra, then 3 hours by road.

items.name: Tiger Hill sunrise
items.summary: Sunrise over Kangchenjunga, with Everest visible on clear days.
items.expect: Leave around 4 am; crowded and cold.
items.tip: Go in October or November for clear skies.

items.name: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway
items.summary: UNESCO narrow-gauge "toy train", with a steam joy ride to Ghum and the Batasia Loop.
items.tip: Take the steam joy ride.

items.name: Happy Valley Tea Estate
items.summary: Old tea estate with tours of the factory and tastings.
items.expect: Closed Mondays; factory runs in season.
items.tip: Visit March to November when leaves are processed.

items.name: Chowrasta and the Mall
items.summary: Ridge-top square and promenade with mountain views.
items.tip: Have tea at Keventer's or Glenary's.

items.name: Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park and HMI
items.summary: Zoo with red pandas and snow leopards, beside the Everest museum of Tenzing Norgay's institute.
items.tip: Combine both.

items.name: Ghoom Monastery
items.summary: Tibetan Buddhist monastery with a large Maitreya Buddha.
items.tip: Combine with the toy train ride.

items.name: Japanese Peace Pagoda
items.summary: White stupa with mountain views and drumming prayers.
items.tip: Go for the evening prayers.

items.name: Momos and thukpa
items.summary: Tibetan dumplings and noodle soup.
items.tip: Try pork or veg momos with chilli.

items.name: Glenary's
items.summary: Colonial bakery and tearoom on the Mall with valley views.
items.tip: Have tea and a pastry on the terrace.

items.name: Keventer's
items.summary: Old breakfast spot with a rooftop over the town.
items.tip: Order the sausage platter.

cashTip: UPI is everywhere but foreign cards may not link; carry rupees for small places and taxis. Tip about 10 percent in restaurants.
name: Leh (Ladakh)
tagline: High-desert monasteries and the roof of India
summary: Leh is the capital of Ladakh, a high-altitude desert of Tibetan Buddhist monasteries, prayer flags and moonscape mountains at 3,500 m. Acclimatise slowly, then visit Thiksey and Hemis monasteries, drive over one of the world's highest roads to the Nubra Valley's dunes and Bactrian camels, and see the colour-shifting Pangong Lake.
seasonNote: June to September; road passes close in winter. Rest your first two days for the altitude.
arrival: Flights from Delhi take 1h20; road access from Manali or Srinagar in summer.
gettingAround: Hire a car with driver; Inner Line Permits are needed for Nubra and Pangong (arranged in Leh).
foodTip: Thukpa, momos, skyu (pasta stew), butter tea and apricots.
buyTip: Pashmina, thangka paintings and dried apricots.

items.name: Leh Palace and old town
items.summary: Nine-storey 17th-century palace above mud-brick lanes.
items.expect: Small fee; climb carefully at altitude.
items.tip: Go up for sunset over the valley.

items.name: Shanti Stupa
items.summary: White stupa on a hill with a panorama of Leh and the mountains.
items.tip: Drive up and walk down.

items.name: Thiksey Monastery
items.summary: Monastery stacked up a hill, with morning prayers and a giant Maitreya Buddha.
items.tip: Arrive at 6 am for the morning puja.

items.name: Hemis Monastery
items.summary: Ladakh's richest monastery, home to a famous mask festival in June or July.
items.tip: Time it with the Hemis Festival.

items.name: Nubra Valley
items.summary: High-desert valley with sand dunes and Bactrian camels, over the high Khardung La pass.
items.tip: Stay in Hunder; ride a camel at sunset.

items.name: Pangong Lake
items.summary: High lake that shifts from turquoise to deep blue, stretching into Tibet.
items.expect: Permit; 5 hours each way; very cold at night.
items.tip: Stay overnight at Spangmik.

items.name: Magnetic Hill and the confluence
items.summary: Optical-illusion road and the meeting of the Indus and Zanskar rivers.
items.tip: Combine with Likir and Alchi monasteries.

items.name: Thukpa and momos
items.summary: Noodle soup and dumplings, warming at altitude.
items.tip: Ask for mutton momos.

items.name: Butter tea and apricots
items.summary: Salty butter tea and sweet local apricots and apricot jam.
items.tip: Buy apricots from the bazaar.

items.name: Skyu
items.summary: Thick stew of thumb-pressed pasta, vegetables and meat.
items.tip: Ask your homestay to make it.

cashTip: UPI is everywhere but foreign cards may not link; carry rupees for small places and taxis. Tip about 10 percent in restaurants.
name: Hampi
tagline: Ruins of an empire among giant boulders
summary: Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, one of the richest cities in the 1500s. Today its temples, palaces and bazaars lie scattered among surreal boulder hills and banana plantations. See the stone chariot at the Vittala Temple, the living Virupaksha Temple, and climb Matanga Hill for sunrise.
seasonNote: November to February; it is fiercely hot from March to May.
arrival: Overnight trains from Bengaluru or Goa to Hosapete, then 30 minutes by auto-rickshaw.
gettingAround: Bicycle, scooter or auto-rickshaw between the ruins.
foodTip: South Indian thalis on banana leaves, dosas and filter coffee.
buyTip: Lambani embroidery from the nearby craft villages.

items.name: Vittala Temple and Stone Chariot
items.summary: Temple with the famous stone chariot and musical pillars.
items.expect: Paid; electric buggies from the gate.
items.tip: Go at opening for soft light and few people.

items.name: Virupaksha Temple
items.summary: Living temple with a tall gopuram and a temple elephant.
items.tip: See the inverted image of the tower in a dark chamber.

items.name: Matanga Hill sunrise
items.summary: Boulder climb to a temple at the top with a sunrise over the ruins.
items.tip: Start 45 minutes before sunrise.

items.name: Royal Enclosure and Lotus Mahal
items.summary: Palace platforms, stepped tank, Lotus Mahal and the Elephant Stables.
items.tip: Use a bike between sites.

items.name: Hemakuta Hill
items.summary: Rock hill of small temples above the bazaar.
items.tip: Sunset spot close to town.

items.name: Coracle ride on the Tungabhadra
items.summary: Round basket-boat ride between the boulders.
items.tip: Agree the price before.

items.name: Hampi Bazaar and Achyutaraya Temple
items.summary: Ruined bazaar street leading to a quiet temple under Matanga Hill.
items.tip: Walk from the Virupaksha end.

items.name: Banana-leaf thali
items.summary: Rice with sambar, rasam, curries and chutneys on a banana leaf.
items.tip: Eat with your right hand.

items.name: Dosa and filter coffee
items.summary: Crisp dosa with coconut chutney, then strong filter coffee.
items.tip: Try a masala dosa.

items.name: Riverside cafés
items.summary: Laid-back cafés with floor cushions and travellers' food.
items.expect: Check which side of the river is open.
items.tip: Watch sunset from a rooftop.

cashTip: UPI is everywhere but foreign cards may not link; carry rupees for small places and taxis. Tip about 10 percent in restaurants.
name: Munnar
tagline: Rolling tea hills of the Western Ghats
summary: Munnar is a cool hill station in Kerala, wrapped in endless emerald tea plantations. Walk among the tea bushes, learn how tea is made at the Tata Tea Museum, spot the rare Nilgiri tahr in Eravikulam National Park, and catch misty sunrise views from Kolukkumalai, one of the highest tea estates in the world.
seasonNote: September to March; monsoon (June to August) is lush but wet. Eravikulam closes in the tahr calving season (about February to March).
arrival: Kochi airport is about 4 hours by road.
gettingAround: Hire a car or jeep with driver; roads are winding.
foodTip: Kerala sadhya, appam with stew, and fresh cardamom tea.
baseArea: Near Munnar town or a tea-estate homestay

items.name: Tea plantation walk
items.summary: Walk the trimmed rows of tea bushes over the hills.
items.tip: Hire a guide for estate trails.

items.name: Eravikulam National Park
items.summary: Grasslands home to the Nilgiri tahr mountain goat.
items.expect: Paid; closed in calving season; bus only.
items.tip: Go early for tahr sightings.

items.name: Tata Tea Museum
items.summary: Museum showing how tea is processed, with a working factory demo.
items.tip: Taste the teas at the end.

items.name: Kolukkumalai sunrise
items.summary: One of the world's highest tea estates, reached by jeep for sunrise above the clouds.
items.expect: Very bumpy jeep ride; early start.
items.tip: Book the jeep the night before.

items.name: Mattupetty Dam and Echo Point
items.summary: Lake and dam with boating among the tea hills.
items.tip: Go on a weekday.

items.name: Top Station
items.summary: Viewpoint on the Kerala-Tamil Nadu border over the valley.
items.tip: Go early.

items.name: Kerala sadhya
items.summary: Vegetarian feast of many dishes on a banana leaf.
items.tip: Eat with your hand, finish with payasam.

items.name: Appam and stew
items.summary: Lacy rice pancakes with coconut-milk stew.
items.tip: Order chicken or vegetable stew.

items.name: Cardamom tea
items.summary: Fresh highland tea brewed with cardamom at roadside stalls.
items.tip: Buy loose tea to take home.
